title: Parameterized coefficient bad set
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$, let $\mathcal F$ be a finite family of subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let $a,c$ be rational parameters with $0<a,c\le 1/2$. For $S\in\mathcal F$, the bad set consists of sample arrays assigning to every member of $\mathcal F$ a batch of $m$ cube inputs, where $m$ is the estimator sample count for $(a,c)$, such that the absolute difference between the empirical Fourier coefficient of $f$ on $S$ from its assigned batch and the true Fourier coefficient of $f$ on $S$ is at least $a$.
hypotheses_covered: $\mathcal F$ is a finite family of subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$
